title: Trade Policy Uncertainty and Investment
abstract: We study how trade policy uncertainty affects firm-level investment. Using panel data and a difference-in-differences strategy, we document a decline in capital expenditures and a shift toward cash holdings.

title: Platforms, Pricing, and Network Effects
abstract: This paper develops a model of platform pricing with multi-sided network effects and empirical estimates from a large online marketplace. We highlight the role of cross-group elasticities.

title: Innovation Spillovers in Digital Markets
abstract: We quantify innovation spillovers between digital firms using patent citations and product releases. Our results show strong complementarities and strategic disclosure.

title: Labor Market Polarization and Automation
abstract: We combine task-level data with firm adoption of automation to evaluate employment polarization. The findings suggest middle-skill job losses and wage dispersion.

title: Consumer Search with Algorithmic Ranking
abstract: We study how algorithmic rankings alter consumer search and market outcomes. The model implies welfare gains but reduced variety for niche products.

title: Privacy Regulation and Advertising Markets
abstract: We measure how privacy regulation changes targeting effectiveness and ad prices. We find short-run revenue declines with partial recovery over time.

title: Entry Barriers in Online Retail
abstract: Using transaction data, we estimate entry barriers and competitive responses in online retail. Results indicate persistent advantages for early movers.

title: Supply Chains and Resilience
abstract: We document how firms reconfigure supply chains after shocks. The analysis highlights diversification as a key resilience mechanism.

title: Education and Remote Learning
abstract: We examine learning outcomes after the adoption of remote platforms. Treatment effects vary across income groups, with widening gaps.

title: Market Power and Innovation
abstract: We relate market power to R&D intensity across industries. The relationship is inverted-U, consistent with the Schumpeterian hypothesis.
